question: Which paper introduced the Transformer architecture, and what was its key idea?
expected_titles: Attention Is All You Need
notes: Landmark paper; high citation count, well-indexed on all sources.
expected_answer: Vaswani et al. (2017) introduced the Transformer architecture based solely on self-attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions.

question: What is retrieval-augmented generation and who proposed it?
expected_titles: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
expected_answer: Lewis et al. (2020) proposed Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), combining pre-trained parametric language models with non-parametric dense vector retrieval.

question: Which paper introduced BERT for language representation?
expected_titles: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
expected_answer: Devlin et al. (2018) introduced BERT, pre-training deep bidirectional representations using masked language modeling and next sentence prediction.

question: Which paper introduced deep residual learning and skip connections in CNNs?
expected_titles: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
expected_answer: He et al. (2015) introduced deep residual learning (ResNet) using identity shortcut connections to solve vanishing gradients in very deep CNNs.

question: Which paper proposed the Adam optimizer for stochastic gradient descent?
expected_titles: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization
expected_answer: Kingma and Ba (2014) introduced Adam, an adaptive learning rate optimization algorithm combining AdaGrad and RMSProp with first and second moment estimation.

question: Who introduced generative adversarial networks?
expected_titles: Generative Adversarial Nets
expected_answer: Goodfellow et al. (2014) introduced Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) using a minimax two-player game between a generator and a discriminator.

question: Which paper introduced LoRA for parameter-efficient fine-tuning of large language models?
expected_titles: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
expected_answer: Hu et al. (2021) introduced Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), freezing pre-trained model weights and injecting trainable rank decomposition matrices into attention layers.

question: Which paper introduced Vision Transformers (ViT) applying self-attention directly to image patches?
expected_titles: An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Transformers for Image Recognition at Scale
expected_answer: Dosovitskiy et al. (2020) introduced Vision Transformer (ViT), treating image patches directly as tokens processed by standard Transformer encoders.

question: Which paper introduced Latent Diffusion Models for high-resolution image synthesis?
expected_titles: High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models
expected_answer: Rombach et al. (2022) introduced Latent Diffusion Models (Stable Diffusion), applying diffusion processes in the compressed latent space of a pre-trained autoencoder.

question: How does CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing repair double-strand breaks in eukaryotic cells?
expected_titles: A Programmable Dual-RNA-Guided DNA Endonuclease in Adaptive Bacterial Immunity
notes: Non-ML biology query for domain generalization test.
expected_answer: CRISPR-Cas9 introduces targeted double-strand breaks repaired by non-homologous end joining (NHEJ, error-prone) or homology-directed repair (HDR, precise template-based).

question: What were the main findings of the GPT-3 paper on few-shot learners?
expected_titles: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
expected_answer: Brown et al. (2020) demonstrated that scaling autoregressive language models to 175 billion parameters enables competitive few-shot learning without task-specific gradient updates.

question: How does retrieval-augmented generation compare to fine-tuning for knowledge-intensive NLP tasks?
expected_titles: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
expected_answer: RAG allows dynamic, source-grounded knowledge updates and verifiable citations with lower retraining costs, while fine-tuning specializes model style, task formats, and domain terminology.

question: What are the main types of attention mechanisms used in modern neural networks?
expected_titles: Attention Is All You Need
Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate
notes: Survey-type question requiring synthesis from multiple papers.
expected_answer: Key attention types include dot-product self-attention, multi-head attention, cross-attention, local windowed/sparse attention, and linear attention approximations.

question: What are the key differences between DDPM, DDIM, and score-based diffusion models?
expected_titles: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
Denoising Diffusion Implicit Models
Score-Based Generative Modeling through Stochastic Differential Equations
notes: Multi-paper comparative; tests conflicting evidence handling.
expected_answer: DDPM uses discrete-time Markov chains; DDIM uses non-Markovian deterministic sampling for accelerated generation; score-based models formulate diffusion via continuous stochastic differential equations (SDEs).

question: Which paper introduced graph convolutional networks for semi-supervised classification?
expected_titles: Semi-Supervised Classification with Graph Convolutional Networks
expected_answer: Kipf and Welling (2016) introduced Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) using a localized first-order approximation of spectral graph convolutions.

question: How does AlphaFold2 predict protein 3D structure from amino acid sequence?
expected_titles: Highly accurate protein structure prediction with AlphaFold
notes: Cross-domain biology + AI paper; tests non-arXiv retrieval.
expected_answer: Jumper et al. (2021) developed AlphaFold2, using Evoformer neural blocks and an invariant point attention structure module to predict 3D protein coordinates directly from multiple sequence alignments.

question: What technique does FlashAttention use to make self-attention IO-efficient?
expected_titles: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness
notes: Systems-level ML optimization; tests technical domain specificity.
expected_answer: Dao et al. (2022) introduced FlashAttention, using tiling and kernel fusion to compute exact softmax self-attention within fast SRAM, drastically reducing GPU HBM memory reads/writes.

question: How is reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) used to align language models?
expected_titles: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback
Learning to summarize from human feedback
expected_answer: Christiano et al. / Ouyang et al. (InstructGPT) use pairwise human preference ratings to train a reward model, which guides reinforcement learning with PPO to align model outputs.

question: What experiment demonstrated quantum computational supremacy and how was it achieved?
expected_titles: Quantum supremacy using a programmable superconducting processor
expected_answer: Arute et al. (2019) demonstrated quantum supremacy using Google's 53-qubit Sycamore superconducting processor to sample random quantum circuits faster than classical supercomputers.

question: Which paper introduced SimCLR for contrastive self-supervised learning of visual representations?
expected_titles: A Simple Framework for Contrastive Learning of Visual Representations
expected_answer: Chen et al. (2020) introduced SimCLR, optimizing a normalized temperature-scaled cross-entropy loss (NT-Xent) over augmented views of images with large batch sizes.

question: What are the main techniques for reducing memory and latency in large language model inference?
expected_titles: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness
Efficiently Scaling Transformer Inference
Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention
expected_answer: Core inference optimization techniques include post-training quantization (INT8/INT4), KV-cache paging and compression (vLLM), speculative decoding, and FlashAttention IO-tiling.

question: How do sparse attention patterns in Longformer differ from the full attention in the original Transformer?
expected_titles: Longformer: The Long-Document Transformer
notes: Tests subtle technical distinction; ambiguous evidence risk.
expected_answer: Beltagy et al. (2020) introduced Longformer, combining local sliding-window attention with task-motivated global attention to scale self-attention linearly with sequence length.

question: What role does molecular dynamics simulation play in protein folding research?
notes: Non-ML domain with sparse open-access coverage; triggers coverage warning.
expected_answer: Molecular dynamics numerically integrates Newton's equations of motion to simulate atomic trajectories over time, revealing intermediate conformational states in protein folding.

question: What do the Chinchilla scaling laws say about optimal model and dataset sizes?
expected_titles: Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models
notes: Tests DeepMind paper retrieval (less on arXiv than others).
expected_answer: Hoffmann et al. (2022) established Chinchilla scaling laws, showing that model parameters and training tokens should scale in equal proportion, proving previous models like GPT-3 were undertrained.

question: How does knowledge distillation from a large teacher model improve a smaller student model?
expected_titles: Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network
notes: Hinton et al. classic; tests model compression domain.
expected_answer: Hinton et al. (2015) introduced knowledge distillation, training a smaller student network using soft target probabilities produced by an ensemble or large teacher model at an elevated temperature.

question: Which paper introduced sparse mixture-of-experts layers for scaling language models?
expected_titles: Switch Transformers: Scaling to Trillion Parameter Models with Simple and Efficient Sparsity
expected_answer: Shazeer et al. (2017) and Fedus et al. (Switch Transformer) introduced sparsely-gated Mixture-of-Experts layers, routing input tokens to specialized sub-networks to scale parameters with constant compute.

question: How do masked language modeling and causal language modeling differ in self-supervised NLP pre-training?
expected_titles: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
notes: Comparative; requires synthesis from BERT and GPT-3 papers.
expected_answer: Masked language modeling (BERT) is bidirectional and predicts randomly corrupted tokens, whereas causal language modeling (GPT) is autoregressive and predicts the next token from left to right.

question: What causes hallucination in large language models and how can it be mitigated?
notes: Survey; conflicting evidence from multiple authors; ambiguous literature.
expected_answer: Hallucination stems from imperfect training data, parametric memory drift, exposure bias, and overconfidence; it is mitigated by retrieval grounding (RAG), NLI entailment auditing, and RLHF calibration.

question: What are the main differences between short-read and long-read DNA sequencing technologies?
notes: Non-ML biology; sparse open access; tests domain generalization.
expected_answer: Short-read sequencing (Illumina) provides high accuracy and high throughput for small variants, while long-read sequencing (PacBio, Oxford Nanopore) spans repetitive regions, structural variants, and complex genomes.

question: What techniques are used in neural architecture search to automate model design?
expected_titles: Neural Architecture Search with Reinforcement Learning
DARTS: Differentiable Architecture Search
expected_answer: Neural architecture search employs reinforcement learning, evolutionary algorithms, and differentiable continuous relaxation (DARTS) over defined search spaces to discover optimal neural network topographies.
